feat(docs): static examples are editable cards, output re-rendered in the browser (rich-example-card-obsb.lz3)

A static docs example is now a <RichExample> card. At rest it is the page's
own card: the build's highlighted fence over the output it printed, rendered
on the server. Hydration moves nothing, and the at-rest screenshots are
byte-identical to the old markup in both colour modes. Clicking into the code
swaps in CodeMirror at the fence's exact box. Once typing pauses (250 ms) the
card runs its setup plus the edited block in a sandboxed worker and redraws
the output. A throw, exit or timeout leaves the last good output dimmed, with
the reason in red under it.

- example-fragments.ts: the one bytes -> light/dark HTML step, used by the
  build and the card.
- theme/sandbox.ts: frame + worker moved out of live-terminal.ts. Its second
  consumer is theme/static-run.ts, which captures a program's bytes under
  STATIC_RUN_LIMIT_MS and reports finished / threw / exited / timedOut /
  stopped.
- example-card.ts: the card's data and cardSource. The build runs the card's
  composition of each static block and holds it to the page's bytes
  (tryItPrints).
- virtual:rich-live/library serves the live library to the card.
- createEditor takes the chrome its caller shows; PROGRAM_PANE is the
  playground's.

fix(progress): progress.percentage magenta and progress.elapsed yellow, as Rich's (rich-progress-rihd) (#350)
